content.text: The verifier's substantive commentary confirms the finding on every point; the only "failure" is a deterministic carve-out check that is unsatisfiable when no non-solicit clause exists. Adding a redline would be wrong here — it would import a restriction on us that the contract does not contain. I'll resubmit the compliant finding with a tightened rationale.

input.quote: c. Limitation on Access. Client will use reasonable commercial efforts consistent with the protection of Client Proprietary Information to restrict access to the Interface to its officers, employees, and agents as may be approved by Client.
input.rationale: No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds Client anywhere in this Agreement, which matches our preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), so no redline or comment is proposed and the fallback narrowing edits are correctly not applied. Literal and regex searches for "solicit", "solicitation", "no-hire", "poach", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel", "staff" and "leave the employ" return only § 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail), incidental "employees" references in the § 12 indemnities, and § 8(c) as quoted, where "employees" appears solely in an access-restriction covenant and imposes no hiring restraint. Full reads of the two candidate locations, § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client, p0050-p0058) and § 10 (Confidentiality, p0061-p0068), confirm the absence. § 8(d) (p0054) cross-references a separate "Non-Competition Agreement" only as a limitation on TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data, not as a restraint on hiring. The failed deterministic checks (duration of 12 months or less; general-solicitation carve-out) are artifacts of there being no clause to measure rather than defects, since a carve-out cannot exist without a covenant to carve out of. Reviewer note: the separate Non-Competition Agreement is outside this document and should be diligenced separately for any hiring restriction binding us.
